knowledge_point.title: Finding the Surface Area of a Parametric Surface

question.:question/problem:
Find the surface area of the parametric surface

$$
\mathbf r(u,v)=\langle 2 u - 2 v - 2,u - 2 v + 2,- 3 u + 3 v - 1\rangle.
$$

For $0\le u\le 3$ and $-1\le v\le 1$.
question.:question/worked-solution:
For a parametrization over $D$, use $$
A(S)=\iint_D\|\mathbf r_u\times\mathbf r_v\|\,\mathrm dA
$$

Differentiate and form the fundamental vector product:

$$
\begin{aligned}
\mathbf r_u&=\langle 2,1,-3\rangle,\\\mathbf r_v&=\langle -2,-2,3\rangle,\\\mathbf r_u\times\mathbf r_v&=\begin{vmatrix}\mathbf i&\mathbf j&\mathbf k\\2&1&-3\\-2&-2&3\end{vmatrix}\\&=\langle -3,0,-2\rangle.
\end{aligned}
$$

$$
\|\mathbf r_u\times\mathbf r_v\|=\sqrt{(-3)^2+(0)^2+(-2)^2}=\sqrt{13}.
$$

The parameter rectangle has side lengths $3-(0)=3$ and $1-(-1)=2$, so its area is $6$.

The area scale factor is constant, so

$$
\begin{aligned}
A(S)&=\iint_D \sqrt{13}\,\mathrm dA\\&=\sqrt{13}\cdot\operatorname{Area}(D)\\&=\sqrt{13}\cdot(6)=6 \sqrt{13}.
\end{aligned}
$$

knowledge_point.title: Finding the Surface Area of a Parametric Surface

question.:question/problem:
Find the surface area of the parametric surface

$$
\mathbf r(u,v)=\langle 2 u,v^{2},\frac{2 v^{3}}{3}\rangle.
$$

For $0\le u\le 2$ and $0\le v\le \sqrt{3}$.
